mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a net improvement from -38.4 at t-3w to -33.4 at t-0w, indicating an underlying recovery trend in discretionary mobility that is expected to persist and push the 4-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC higher than the trailing 4-week mean.
failure_condition: If the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed upward trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below -40 percent of baseline, it signals acute suppression of inter-neighborhood movement, which mechanically reduces the pool of potential shoppers reaching retail and recreation venues within the following two weeks, pulling RETAIL_REC lower.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks following a TRANSIT reading below -40, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent week-on-week improvement in both WORKPLACES (-34.0 to -30.9) and TRANSIT (-40.4 to -38.7) reflects a joint resumption of commuting and transit use that compounds to increase incidental retail footfall, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the following 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility above +10 percent across all four observed weeks indicates an active stay-at-home policy regime that structurally caps discretionary outings, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks as long as the regime holds.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 percent for all weeks in the lookback window
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 9.9 and 13.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp seasonal rebound in PARKS mobility, such as the +21 point jump from -33.1 (t-3w) to -12.1 (t-2w), reflects warmer-weather outdoor activity that is complementary to retail and leisure trips, so continued PARKS strength over the next 2 weeks should coincide with higher RETAIL_REC.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -33.1 to -12.1 between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines over the next 2 weeks despite a PARKS jump greater than 10 points, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays within a narrow band near baseline (roughly -4 to -10) while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +10, it signals a risk-averse behavioral pattern where households limit trips to essentials only, which should depress RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-5 of -8 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged -3.9 to -9.7 and RESIDENTIAL ranged 9.9 to 13.0 across the window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the following week despite stable GROCERY_PHARM and elevated RESIDENTIAL, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility exceeding 5 points, as seen from -26.9 (t-2w) to -34.0 (t-1w), signals a fresh tightening of workplace-related restrictions that quickly spills over to reduce adjacent retail activity within the same or following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -26.9 to -34.0 between t-2w and t-1w
fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -32.3 to -35.9 over the same period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall within the week following a WORKPLACES drop greater than 5 points, the hypothesis is rejected.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained in a narrow -3.9 to -9.7 range across the four weeks
